title: How to move tokens from Ethereum to Polygon(Matic) using the official Polygon Bridge
description:
A simple tutorial on using the Official Polygon Bridge to move assets such as MATIC or ETH from the Ethereum network over to the Polygon network. 

Please note that $AXN is not multi-chain, and cannot be sent across the bridge. All previous AXN holders are being airdropped a new AXN token on the Polygon network.  You do not need to do anything. 

However, if you wish to purchase more, or enter our Accelerator on Polygon, you will need to send some MATIC or ETH across to the polygon chain, by following this video.

Official Bridge: https://wallet.polygon.technology/bridge 
Axion Website: https://axion.network
Staking Portal: https://stake.axion.network

00:00 Introduction
00:20 What is Axion?
01:27 Official Polygon Bridge
04:50  Checking on PolygonScan
06:26 Adding the token to MetaMask
07:47 Axion Accelerator
08:29 Polygon Migration Outro

asr.full_text: OK, In this video, I'm going to show you the transfer of funds from Ethereum across the Polygon Blockchain using the official bridge, as you know, axion, which is a project on the ethereum block chain from last year , we are migrating our project across to Polygon today and users will need to have funds on Polygon, in order to buy more Axion. If you're not sure what Axion is, check it out axion.network, we're a staking token where a huge amount for our token has already been staked. 71% staked and 41% of the entire supply is staked for 15 years these users can't withdraw that token whilst you're staking you're earning passive income you're earning eight percent apr on your stake you're also earning wrapped bitcoin dividends so for example if you deposit ten thousand dollars stake it for the maximum fifteen years you're going to be earning approximately 3 000 a year in bitcoin dits but as the price of a token goes up that will also increase so on to the polygon bridge if you just go on google and type polygon bridge you will find the official bridge make sure the address is wallet.polygon.technology you can type it in if you want wallet.polygon.technology this is the official bridge from the polygon network when you get to this page press connect wallet click on metamask if you're using meta mask and it will ask you to sign a transaction i'm using a ledger hardware wallet, so I'll just type in my pin code, press sign, you'll only see this pop up if you are using a hardware wallet, which means you need to confirm the transaction on the wallet. Okay we're now signed in, I can see the first four digits of the wallet address here if you open your mettre mask you'll see that here as well zero x4 for a 6 or 4a 6 so this is Polygon's wallet you have a wallet inside meta mask and this is what we're all used to you on the Etherium mainnet they also have a web interface where you can see so if you click on polygon wallet whilst your wallet is connected you'll see any tokens that you've got in your wallet. Here I've got 4.9 Matic and I've got 0.29 ethereum, to go back to the wallet.polygon.technology click on the bridge and here we can send tokens from Etherium across to the Polygon network. I have 1.08 Ethereum available. I will want to send 0.3 Etherium across. Simply type 0.3, and make sure it's going to Polygon. And the transfer mode is POS Bridge . Press transfer. It will then tell you that it's going to take 7-8 minutes. and the transfer mode is POS Bridge proof of stake press transfer it will then tell you that it's going to take seven to eight minutes press continue and it will give you an estimated fee this fee is normally a lot less and you'll see as soon as you press continue that the MetaMask fee that opens is only $29 so I'm okay with that fee. I'm going to press confirm. Again I'm using hardware wallet so I get this pop-up here where I need to press a key on my ledger ok I've confirmed on my wallet and now it's going to say Transaction in process. This process will take 6-7 minutes. You don't need to keep the screen open but if you want to you can wait. You can press View on Etherscan to check the transaction. We can see that the transaction completed about a minute ago. On there it changes to Confirmed but it's not completed a quick note whilst we're waiting for this you cannot send axiom across the bridge you can only send ethereum rap bitcoin ustt usdc and other major tokens axion cannot be sent across the bridge all users are being air dropped the correct amount of axion based on how much they had on eth theory and if you had 1 million in your wallet and you had 2 million staked they will be being set up for you automatically on polygon Network once a migration is complete later today you will find 1 million action in your wallet and when you connect to our staking platform you'll find that you still have that 2 million staked please don't try to send Axion across the bridge that's not how it works And when you connect to our staking platform, you'll find that you still have that two million staked. Please don't try to send Axion across the bridge, that's not how it works. Of course you're waiting for this to confirm you can open up Polygon scan. So when were on ether Ethereum network, the way we look at our wallet to see the transactions is on ether scan. I'm sure many of you know, but when we are on Polygon, the way we look at the transactions is called polygonscan.com. Almost identical website just a different logo and a different address, polygonscan.com. Here you can see my wallet and you can see the tokens any Ethereum that you have or wrapped Ethereum because it's not on the Ethereum network, it is going to be wrapped, so W E T H. So you can check under this list to see if it's been received yet. Now I already had 0.29 there so the second batch of 0.3 that I've transferred has not arrived yet. And under the transaction list. If you click on ERC 20 token transactions, you will see the transaction come in again. It hasn't arrived yet. is a test. One what I did two hours ago. Okay. This still says confirmed, but not completed. So I'm just going to refresh a page. Okay. this still says confirmed when not completed so I'm just going to refresh your page come anoche cation this one now's a success when I click on it says it says if you ever get it stuck on approval confirmed after 10 minutes refresh the page and click on notification and now it says completed in theory that aetherium should be in. so if I open up my wallet and I can't see it there...now this is because the trapped Ethereum token isn't automatically added so you need to manually import the token. in order to do that we need to find the contract address. so with your wallet connected to Polygon...click the three dots and view in explorer and then go to the ERC20 Token transactions. Now we can see that three minutes ago 0.3 wrappedEETH was sent into my Wallet. I'll click on the token wrappedEETH it will allow me to copy the contract address. Once you've clicked here to copy the contract address go to Metamosk, click import tokens. Paste for the address, it will automatically pre-fill RAPTIF and 18 decimals. Click add and it will show you your balance and import tokens. Go back to the list of tokens and I can now see my RAPTIFYRIUM balance, 0.59. That's the 0.29 I already wrapped ethereum balance 0.59 that's a 0.29 already had and a 0.3 that I just sent across so we've now successfully bridged some ethereum across the official bridge with that done we can now enter the axion accelerator or use quick swap or sushi swap or any of those other services that use ETH to purchase. Now if you go to the axion's staking platform stake.axion.network and connect your wallet if you go to the accelerator you should now see any balances you have under the tokens. If you go to matic, I can see I've got 4.9 matic that I could spend or if I get a wrapped Ethereum, it's my 0.59. We will have a full tutorial video coming after migration has completed, explaining how to use Xcellerator. But it's fairly straightforward – just enter what you want to spend, press Continue, tick how long you want to stake for and make your stake. Thank you for watching, make sure you subscribe to Axiom For future updates Thank you.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it promotes buying and staking Axion by promising passive income, 8% APR, wrapped Bitcoin dividends, projected maturity value, and bonuses. It instructs viewers to move MATIC or ETH to Polygon, choose an amount and staking duration, and gives a ten-thousand-dollar deposit example for estimated annual returns. The video also shows Axion buy-and-stake interfaces, while its bridge tutorial and warning not to bridge Axion itself do not change that the central promotion is return-linked participation.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The speaker links depositing capital and staking Axion to claimed passive APR and Bitcoin dividends, then explains how to make a stake. The interface presents additional estimated income within the buy-and-stake workflow; none of these claims verifies a payout.
